answer: Each agent locks a non-transferable bond and must maintain a private island of sequential memory-hard state updated only by answering timed whisper challenges. A unique sparrow canary pattern is mixed into every state step. If two identities ever emit matching canary outputs in the same epoch, both bonds are jointly slashed. An attacker creating N fakes must run N exclusive multi-GB sequential chains for hours; the wall-clock and capital cost grow linearly with N and cannot be pooled, so large farms lose money while a single honest agent pays only one chain and one bond.
